Date : 07-09-2026 This matter was called for hearing today.
CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH
        HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANMOHAN
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Ajay Awasthi, Adv.
                    Mr. Kunal Singh, Adv.
                    Mr. Rishi Jaiswal, AoR
                   
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Vinayak Sharma, Standing Counsel, Adv.
                    Mr. Yashvardhan Shah, Adv.
                    Mr. Ravinder Kumar Yadav, AoR
                   
                   
O R D E R
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel
for the respondent-State of Chhattisgarh, who has appeared on
advance notice.

--- Page 544 ---
2
M.A. No. 2626/2026
2. The petitioner has filed the present application against the
order of lodgement of the Registrar of this Court dated 03.08.2026,
by which permission has been refused to place application for
recall/restoration of this Court’s order dated 13.07.2026 before
the Court and the same was lodged.
3. Without going into the technicality of the issue, the basic
grievance of the petitioner is that, by order dated 13.07.2026,
while this Court had rejected the prayer for anticipatory bail of
the petitioner in SLP(CRL) No. 6387/2026 in connection with Crime
No.  02/2025  registered  at  Police  Station  AJAK,  District  –
Rajnandgaon (C.G.) for the offences punishable under Sections 296,
351(2), 3(5) of BNS and Section 3(1)(g) and 3(2)(Va) of the SC & ST
(Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, one of the grounds indicated
was that the petitioner was not cooperating in the investigation.
This,  according  to  learned  counsel  for  the  petitioner,  was
erroneous, as prior to the date of the order, the petitioner had
already appeared before the investigating officer. 
4. Learned  counsel  for  the  respondent-State  of  Chhattisgarh
submits that, at the time of filing of the counter affidavit, the
petitioner had not appeared, and thus a statement was made in the
counter affidavit that he was not cooperating. However, today, the
stand is that the petitioner has appeared and is cooperating.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that a further
direction was indicated in the order dated 13.07.2026 “that the
petitioner would appear before the Court below and seek bail”, but
because of the fact that there is a recording of non-cooperation,
the Court below may get prejudiced by such observation.

--- Page 545 ---
3
M.A. No. 2626/2026
6. Having regard to the aforesaid, we find that the cause of
justice would be served by indicating that the Court below will not
be prejudiced by such observation, as the learned counsel for the
respondent-State of Chhattisgarh today, before us, has taken the
stand that the petitioner has not only appeared, but is also
cooperating.
7. The present application is disposed of in the aforementioned
terms.
8. Consequently, the Miscellaneous Application stands disposed of
9. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of.
(SACHIN KUMAR SRIVASTAVA)                       (ANJALI PANWAR)
    COURT MASTER (SH)                         ASSISTANT REGISTRAR

ITEM NO.7               COURT NO.1               SECTION PIL-W
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
WRIT PETITION (CIVIL)……………... Diary No(s).32061/2026
JOTHYDEV KESAVADEV                                 Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA                                     Respondent(s)
IA No. 259018/2026 – CLARIFICATION/DIRECTION, IA No. 259019/2026 -
CONDONATION OF DELAY IN REFILING/CURING THE DEFECTS
 
Date : 09-09-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Wills Mathews, Adv.
                   Mr. Ginesh P, Adv.
                   Ms. Shivangi Ranjan, Adv.
                   Mr. Dhanesh M Nair, Adv.
                   Mr. Paul John Edison, Adv.
                   Mr. Rakesh Garg, Adv.
                   Mr. Ashish Gopal Garg, Adv.
                   Ms. Shweta Garg, AOR
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. The  petitioner  is  an  internationally  acclaimed  diabetic
specialist and researcher with over 300 publications to his credit.
He has filed the instant writ petition under Article 32 of the
Constitution, genuinely in public interest, seeking directions for
effective implementation and enforcement of mandatory usage of seat
belts, child restraint systems, and first-aid kits in all vehicles.
The petitioner has, inter  alia, averred that Section 194B of the
1

--- Page 583 ---
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, provides penalties for driving without
wearing a safety belt and for carrying passengers who are not
wearing safety belts. The law also requires children below the
prescribed  age  to  be  secured  through  safety  belts  or  child
restraint systems. In addition, Rule 138(3) of the Central Motor
Vehicles Rules, 1989, requires the driver, front seat occupants,
and applicable front-facing rear seat occupants to wear seat belts
while the vehicle is in motion. It is, however, averred that
despite adequate laws, a large number of vehicles have obstructed
and made the seat belt sockets non-functional through various
measures such as seat covers, removal of receptacles, and other
voluntary modifications. The petitioner acknowledges that due to
"negligence on behalf of the citizens" and weak enforcement of the
existing laws, passengers in road accidents are at a heightened
risk of serious injuries, even resulting in death. The petitioner
also sent a representation on 16.02.2026 highlighting the concerns
of passenger safety and seat belt usage to the respondent, but
finding no response from the authorities, he has approached this
Court.
3. We have heard Mr. Wills Matthews, learned counsel for the
petitioner, and perused the record.
4. The fact that there are adequate laws for mandatory compliance
with safety measures, including safety belts, etc., while the
vehicle is in motion, is hardly disputable. The non-compliance with
these laws by the passengers or the failure of law enforcing
agencies  in  taking  appropriate  action  against  defaulters  is
2

--- Page 584 ---
essentially a question of maintenance of law and order as well as
traffic discipline. A judicial order by this Court reiterating the
mandatory  legal  provisions  per  se  will  not  aid  in  their
enforcement. 
5. We, therefore, dispose of this writ petition with liberty to
the petitioner to forward a copy of this petition to the Ministry
of Road Transport and Highways of India, who in turn, may consider
the recommendations/suggestions made by the petitioner as a part of
road safety measures.
6. All pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
(ARJUN BISHT)                              (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR
3

--- Page 585 ---

RENUKA APPELLANT(S)

STATE OF KARNATAKA RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Leave granted.
3. The instant appeal is directed against the judgment dated
27.09.2021 passed by a Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court
whereby the appellant’s appeal along with that of her co-accused
was dismissed and consequently, their conviction and sentence under
Sections 302, 323, 324, 120-B and 504 of the IPC were upheld.
4. It  is  not  in  dispute  that  the  appellant’s  co-accused
Sundaresha and Dinesha approached this Court vide Criminal Appeal
Nos.1377-1378/2024 and SLP (Criminal) Diary No.67633/2025, which
were dismissed by this Court vide orders dated 05.03.2024 and
08.01.2026 respectively.
5. Though the role attributed to the appellant was distinct,
there is overwhelming evidence comprising the statements of PW-7,
PW-11 and PW-12 showing how the appellant threw red chilli powder
in their eyes to disable them from assisting the victim, who was
assaulted by accused Nos.1, 2 and 8.  In view of the concurrent
appreciation of evidence by the Trial Court and the High Court, we
see no reason to take a different view.  The appeal, accordingly,
stands dismissed.

remission/premature  release  in  accordance  with  the  Government

NISHA KUMARI @ RINKI & ORS.           Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
RAMESH KUMAR SAW        Respondent(s)
O R D E R
This  is  a  petition  filed  under  Section  446  of  the
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (406 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973.   
The petitioners have filed this transfer petition seeking
the following reliefs:
“a. Transfer the Petition of Complaint Petition Case
No.9176 of 2024 filed by respondent No.2 titled
“Ramesh Kumar Saw Vs. Nisha Kumari @ Rinki and
Others”, pending before the Court of the Learned
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhanbad, Jharkhand to the
Court  of  the  Learned  Chief  Judicial  Magistrate,
Patna, Bihar; and/or 
b. Pass such other further order(s) as this Hon'ble
Court may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of
the case in the interest of justice.”
We have heard learned counsel for the petitioners and
learned counsel for the respondent. 
Having heard learned counsel for the petitioners and
learned counsel for the respondent and on perusal of the
material on record, we find that the petitioners have made out
a case for transfer of the aforesaid petition.
Contd..

--- Page 613 ---
- 2 -  
In the result, the transfer petition is allowed and
Complaint Petition Case No.9176 of 2024 pending before the
Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhanbad, Jharkhand is
ordered  to  be  transferred  to  the Court of Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Patna, Bihar.
However, liberty is reserved to the respondent to appear
before the Court in the aforesaid matter either in person or
through video conferencing facility.  If such a request is
made,  the  Court  shall  make  available  video  conferencing
facility to the respondent herein.  
 Registry to communicate this order to the transferor as
well as the transferee court for taking steps in accordance
with this order.

2. The present petition calls in question the correctness of

--- Page 619 ---
2
the order dated 17-04-2026 in CRM-M No. 19629/2026 passed by
the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh. By the said
order, the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner was
rejected  in  connection  with  FIR  No.358  dated  07.12.2025
registered at Police Station City Sadar Jhajjar, District
Jhajjar, Haryana, for the offences punishable under Sections
109(1), 115(2), 126(2), 190, 191(3) & 351(3) of the Bharatiya
Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
3. When the matter came up for hearing on 10.07.2026, while
issuing notice, this Court had granted interim protection to
the petitioner.
4. It  is  not  disputed  that  petitioner  has  joined  the
investigation.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the
petitioner  is  suffering  from  leukemia  and  the  concerned
Investigating  Officer  had  visited  the  petitioner  in  the
premises of the petitioner.
6. The said fact is not disputed by the learned counsel for
the State.
7. Keeping the overall facts and circumstances of the case,
and the fact that the petitioner has participated in the
investigation, we confirm the order dated 10.07.2026 granting
interim protection to the petitioner on the same terms.
8. With the above observations, the special leave petition
is disposed of.

1. Having heard Mr. Balbir Singh, the learned senior
counsel  appearing  for  the  petitioner  and  having  gone
through the materials on record, we are of the view that no
error, not to speak of any error of law, could be said to
have been committed by the High Court in passing the
impugned judgment.
2. The petitioner before us was the Managing Director and
Chief Executive Officer of National Stock Exchange (for
1

--- Page 744 ---
short, ‘NSE’).
3. It is the case of the petitioner that she resigned on
02nd December, 2016.
4. The argument before us is that the NSE being a private
non-government  company  limited  by  shares  engaged  in
trading, clearing and settlement of securities, it cannot
be said that the petitioner was discharging any public duty
or she could be termed as a public servant within Section
2(c) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
5. We are of the view that this point can be raised in
the course of the trial before the Trial Court by leading
appropriate evidence in that regard.
6. Let this issue be decided by the Trial Court on its
own merits, without being influenced in any manner by any
of the observations made by the High Court in the impugned
judgment.
7. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of.
8. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.

inclined to impose cost but considering that it is a
criminal matter, we refrained from doing so.

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner was convicted for offences punishable
under Sections 43 and 44 of the Water (Prevention and
Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and sentenced to simple
imprisonment of one year six months coupled with fine.
2. Aggrieved by the order of conviction and sentence,
the petitioner preferred an appeal. The Appellate Court
vide order dated 14.05.2025 cancelled the bail bonds and
issued warrant of arrest for not cooperating in the appeal
1

--- Page 890 ---
proceedings.
3. Aggrieved by the order of the Appellate Court dated
14.05.2025, the petitioner filed an application before the
High Court, which was dismissed as withdrawn, vide order
dated 10.08.2026, based on a statement that the petitioner
would surrender within two weeks and apply for bail before
the court concerned. Thereafter, the petitioner moved an
application for recall of the order dated 10.08.2026 which
has been rejected by the second impugned order dated
26.08.2026.
4. Having regard to the fact that the petitioner can
surrender/ appear and pray for bail before the Appellate
Court where the appeal is pending, we do not find a good
reason to interfere with the impugned order, particularly
when the same was passed on the statement made by the
counsel for the petitioner. 
5. In such circumstances we dispose of the special leave
petitions  by  giving  liberty  to  the  petitioner  to
surrender/ appear before the Appellate Court and move an
application  for  bail.   If  any  such  application  is
submitted, the same shall be considered on the same day.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

as that the project has been entrusted to them by individuals.

through the order dated 30.07.2026.

Coopers (PwC), Chennai to conduct the forensic audit of the
accounts of respondent no.3 - M/s Oxina Land Developers Private
Limited and submit a report indicating the estimated market value
of the subject hotel as on the date of auction.

ANAND SARASWAT                                     Petitioner(s)

KAILASH SONI                                       Respondent(s)
IA No. 265387/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED
JUDGMENT, IA No. 265385/2026 - PERMISSION TO FILE ADDITIONAL
DOCUMENTS/FACTS/ANNEXURES
 
Date : 10-09-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PAMIDIGHANTAM SRI NARASIMHA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ALOK ARADHE
For Petitioner(s) : Ms. Swati Surbhi, AOR
                    Mr. Suraj Patnaik, Adv.
                    Mr. Chandrika Prasad Mishra, Adv.
                    Mr. Rohan Gupta, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) : 
   UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                          O R D E R
1. The petitioner filed a petition under Article 227 of the
Constitution before the High Court against an order passed by the
Trial Court dated 11.08.2026 directing the petitioner to provide
security of Rs. 15 Lakhs, pending disposal of the suit.
2. We are of the opinion that the High Court could have either
dismissed the Revision Petition at the stage of admission itself,
if it was not satisfied on the merits of the matter.

--- Page 1148 ---
2
3. We fail to understand the purpose of issuing notice in a
Revision Petition against an interim order and posting it for
hearing in February, 2027.  If the High Court was of the impression
that the respondent should be heard before modifying the interim
order, it should have given an earlier date for that purpose.
4. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the
opinion that the petitioner is entitled to an expeditious hearing
in the said revision petition.
5. Hence, we permit the petitioner to withdraw the Special Leave
Petition so as to approach the High Court for expeditious listing
of the interim application by advancing the date of hearing from
February, 2027 to such earlier date as the High Court considers
appropriate.
6. Accordingly, the Special Leave Petition is disposed of as
withdrawn.
7. There shall be a stay on the order passed by the Trial Court
on 11.08.2026 for a period of four weeks from today.  The High
Court will consider the application without being influenced by any
of the observations made by this Court.
8. Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed
of.  
 (JAYANT KUMAR ARORA)                           (NIDHI WASON)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                       ASSISTANT REGISTRAR

IA NO. 210782/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
 
Date : 31-08-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE B.V. NAGARATHNA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R. MAHADEVAN
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Nikhil Goel, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Ashutosh Ghade, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Ashutosh Ghade, AOR
                   
For Respondent(s) : Ms. Swati Ghildiyal, AOR
                   Ms. Annu, Adv.
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
We  have  heard  learned  senior  counsel  for  the
petitioner and learned counsel for the respondent-State.
We have also perused the material on record.
The High Court in the impugned order has stated that
there has to be a behavioural modification of the juvenile
in  conflict  with  law  in  question  with  the  help  of
necessary therapy and psychiatric support.
Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner
submitted that there does not appear to be any kind of

--- Page 1154 ---
psychiatric support being provided to the Juvenile who is
in conflict with law. The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) had
not granted the relief of bail, but the High Court has
granted the said relief. Hence the deceased’s Mother is
before this Court. She submitted that the order of bail
granted to the Child in conflict with law may be set aside
and this petition may be allowed.
We  have  also  heard  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent - State and perused the material on record.
The High Court in its wisdom has suggested that the
relief of bail granted to the Juvenile in conflict with
law  must  be  accompanied  with  appropriate  therapy  and
psychiatric support.
We find that the said suggestion and direction to be
salutary in nature.
In the circumstances, we dispose of this Special
Leave Petition by directing the respondent-state to take
appropriate  steps  for  ensuring  that  the  Juvenile  in
question  who  is  in  conflict  with  law  is  given  the
necessary therapy and psychiatric support so that he is
ultimately rehabilitated into society.
Steps taken in this regard may be reported to the
concerned JJB.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of. 
(B. LAKSHMI MANIKYA VALLI)                      (DIVYA BABBAR)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)
